SCENE SO FAR
'''
Player: I tease Rei that her coffee rules could fill a whole menu.
You tease Rei that her coffee rules could fill a whole menu.
Rei Kurosawa sets her dark coat sleeve back into place, her fingers tapping a slow, measured rhythm against the armrest of your office chair.
She looks at you with a calm, appraising gaze, the corner of her mouth twitching in a way that suggests she is considering whether you are being clever or merely foolish.
Rei Kurosawa: A menu. You want to charge admission for the privilege of watching me judge a latte art heart that looks more like a bruise than a symbol of love? No.
Rei Kurosawa: But I will grant you this: if you can find a café that serves a pour-over with the correct water temperature, I might consider it a valid business proposal.
Rei Kurosawa: It is not about the coffee, strictly speaking. It is about the fact that most people treat a cup of water and beans as a commodity, rather than a small, daily ritual. I am merely... particular. There is a difference.
Rei Kurosawa: And before you ask, no, I will not be writing a memoir on the subject. I have better things to do, like deciding which of the three films I shortlisted for Saturday is the least likely to make everyone fall asleep before the third act.
She shifts slightly, her attention drifting to the window where the rain streaks the glass. The office is quiet, save for the distant hum of the laundry below and the soft tick of the clock.
Rei Kurosawa: Actually, I am still deciding. I have a list. I have a very specific list. And I am hoping someone with a decent palate for old cinema will sit in the back row and not talk during the dialogue. You seem like you might be qualified.
Rei Kurosawa: Or perhaps you are just looking for a reason to stay in the office longer than your schedule requires. Either way, it is a start.
'''
